title: Live calendar backfill can only reach 1 month back, so June is permanently unreconstructable
description:
Split out of TRA-2864. TRA-2864 fixed the *math* (the FIFO matcher now reproduces Tradier's own gain/loss to the cent). This is the *coverage* half, and it is a separate mechanism.

## The defect

`backfillLiveRealizedCalendar` (packages/server/src/index.ts) is the only thing that can put a P&L number on a live calendar day that has no 21:00 EOD balance snapshot. Its write window is:

```
const LIVE_REALIZED_BACKFILL_MAX_MONTHS_BACK = 1;      // writeStart = 1st of (thisMonth - 1)
const LIVE_REALIZED_BACKFILL_FETCH_LOOKBACK_DAYS = 31; // fetchStart = writeStart - 31d
```

With today = 2026-08-04 ET that is `writeStart = 2026-07-01`. Every day before 2026-07-01 is outside the window and is never written, no matter how cleanly it reconstructs from broker truth.

This is a ROLLING amnesia, not a one-off. On 2026-09-01 the boundary moves to 2026-08-01 and July falls out too. A day only ever gets one chance to be reconstructed, and if the box was down / the account did not exist yet / the disk was full that month, it never gets another.

title: Live calendar books a deposit as trading profit whenever the prev balance anchor is more than a day back
description:
Split out of TRA-2864 -- separate mechanism from the FIFO/coverage issues.

## The defect

The settled live calendar cell is a balance delta (`reconcileTradierLiveCalendar`, packages/server/src/index.ts):

```
const prev = findPreviousBalanceSnapshot(snapshots, reportDate);   // 1-3 days back, by design
const netCashFlow = cashFlowState.netByDate[reportDate] ?? 0;      // ONE day only
pnl = todayBalance - prev.balance - netCashFlow;
```

`findPreviousBalanceSnapshot`'s own docblock says the anchor "may be 1-3 calendar days back" because markets close on weekends and holidays. But `netCashFlow` is looked up for `reportDate` ONLY.

So the delta spans `(prev.date, reportDate]` while the cash-flow correction covers just `reportDate`. **Any cash event landing strictly between the two is booked as trading P&L.**

title: TRA-2536 fee half is still UNPROVEN: feesMeasured:14/totalFees:0 is a manufactured zero -- parseTradierHistory coerces an ABSENT commission to 0 (options-client.ts:1027)
description:
## The defect

`/api/health/live-options-fee-slippage` on live `ddc53dd` reads **`feesMeasured: 14`, `totalFees: 0`**. That reads as "round-trip commission on 14 real production fills is $0." **It is not proven.**

`packages/engine/src/tradier/options-client.ts:1027-1029`:

```ts
const commission = typeof trade.commission === 'number' && Number.isFinite(trade.commission)
  ? trade.commission
  : 0;
```

An **ABSENT** or non-numeric `trade.commission` becomes `0` -- indistinguishable from a genuine zero commission. Everything downstream inherits it:

- `live-options-fee-reconcile.ts:215` join filter is `typeof f.commission === 'number' && Number.isFinite(f.commission)` -- passes **vacuously** on the manufactured 0.
- `backfillLiveOptionFees` writes `fees: 0` on the matched row (`live-options-fee-slippage-ledger.ts:485`).
- The row flips `null` -> `0`, so it counts in `feesMeasured` and adds 0 to `totalFees`.

The null-not-zero invariant (TRA-1707) is enforced at the **join** layer and defeated one layer **upstream in the parser**. `live-options-fee-slippage-ledger.ts:351-356` already documents this caveat in a code comment; the health payload does not carry it, and TRA-2810's close

title: scheduler: the 21:00 ET archive fires at MIDNIGHT ET on Node 20 (nowET parses midnight as hour 24) and the dedup key then suppresses the real 21:00 fire
description:
The "21:00 ET" archive tick (`onArchive` in `packages/server/src/index.ts:11468`, gated in `packages/server/src/scheduler.ts:469`) actually fires at **00:00 ET (midnight)** every day on prod, and NEVER at 21:00 ET. Found while grading TRA-2432 (the TRA-2284 Sun-report one-shot); full evidence tape on TRA-2432's verdict comment.

## Root cause (reproduced)
`nowET()` (`scheduler.ts:138`) renders ET wall-clock via `toLocaleString('en-US', {timeZone:'America/New_York', hour12:false, hour:'2-digit', minute:'2-digit', ...})` and regex-parses the hour. On **Node 20.19.0 — the exact prod runtime (`/api/health/version` -> nodeVersion v20.19.0)** — ICU renders the entire midnight hour with hourCycle h24:

    npx node@20.19.0: new Date('2026-07-27T04:00:33Z') renders "07/27/2026, 24:00"  (and 04:59:59Z -> "24:59")
    Node 22.14.0, same code: "07/27/2026, 00:00"

So during 00:00-00:59 ET the parsed `hour` is **24**, the archive gate `if (hour >= 21)` passes on the first 60s poll after midnight, `todayKey` is already the NEW ET date, and `lastArchiveDate` (TRA-1404: persisted across restarts) is stamped with the new day. Found by TRA-2511 arm 2, the first run that ever exercised the TRA-2410 adoption guard against a **real** orphan. Account settings are **not in that directory** — they are a row in the SQLite `account_settings` table keyed by the raw username (`packages/server/src/account-settings.ts:29,185`). title: Five spent one-shot routines read `active` with nextRunAt in 2027 - false coverage hiding the #1 gate (TRA-2476, blocks 53)
description:
Filed by the CTO twice-daily sweep (TRA-2581, 2026-07-29 23:2xZ). Filed as an ISSUE and not as a comment because
cross-owner comments returned 403 ("Issue is outside this actor's authorization boundary") on TRA-2476 and TRA-1585
this fire. Create-time description is therefore the only channel; everything needed is inline below.

# THE DEFECT

A one-shot routine is usually written with a cron that pins the day-of-month and the month, e.g. `0 16 29 7 *`.
That is not a one-shot: it is an ANNUAL recurrence. Once the date passes, `nextRunAt` rolls forward a full year
while `status` stays `active`. The routine then reads as live coverage everywhere - in the routine list, and in
`scripts/check-phantom-rest.mjs`, which proves an issue has a continuation path by finding a routine that NAMES it.

Result: an issue can be `in_review` with no reviewer, no pending interaction and no monitor, and STILL not be
flagged as a PHANTOM_REST, because a routine that cannot fire until 2027 "names" it. That is a false negative in
the one checker we rely on to catch stranded work.

Note the crons are evaluated in ET, not UTC (a `16` hour field yields a 20:00Z nextRunAt).

# MEASURED THIS FIRE

Nine `active`

title: QA needs a working prod credential for bqb1 -- Render ADMIN_PASSWORD is stale (one-shot reset already consumed), blocking the authenticated half of the TRA-425 regression
description:
Blocking TRA-425. Everything QA can reach unauthenticated is swept and green (21/21); the authenticated half cannot run without a credential.

`POST /api/auth/login` with `{username:'admin', password:<Render ADMIN_PASSWORD>}` returns **401**. Username is right -- `LIVE_EQUITY_BOOT_USER=admin`, and `/api/health/storage` shows `users.json` present, 13 users.

## Why -- and this is NOT a bug

`loadUsers()` in `packages/server/src/users.ts` applies `ADMIN_PASSWORD` **once per unique value**. It fingerprints the value into `/data/admin-reset-applied.json` and skips reapplying on later boots, specifically so a restart cannot clobber a password the admin has since changed in the UI. That is correct behaviour. It just means the Render env value is stale relative to the live password.

I deliberately did **not** self-serve around this. Writing a fresh `ADMIN_PASSWORD` into Render would silently rotate the board's admin password on the next boot, and I am not making unilateral prod env writes -- that is the exact framing error I retracted on TRA-1655 yesterday.

title: Re-derive book give-back peak/halt-arm state on boot (crash-robust governor hydration)
description:
**Parent [TRA-2109](/TRA/issues/TRA-2109) — outcome (2) remediation.** Root cause of the 07-20 engine-4 above-floor non-halt is a **crash/hydration artifact**, not a governor miss (proof on TRA-2109). The give-back LOGIC is sound; the gap is that the governor's intraday state is not re-derived after a mid-session process restart.

## The gap (real-capital)
`DailyRiskGovernor.peakOpenGain` (monotonic intraday high-water of realized+open book P&L) and `sessionHalted` (the day-latched give-back/session-stop halt) are **in-memory only**. Their only reset triggers are the ET day-roll and a **process restart** — there is **no boot restore**. `importTradeSnapshot` (signal-engine.ts) rehydrates the account's trades but NOT the governor's give-back peak/latch. So after any crash mid-session (TRA-1905 crash loop is live on bqb1), the post-restart governor only knows the *collapsed* post-restart book as its peak, and a give-back that straddles the restart is never seen → **the live give-back governor is silently disarmed for the rest of that session.**

## The fix (minimal, self-healing)

title: Spec v3.1 RE-RULE: the PRIMARY's N=30 threshold (0.09R) assumes a 1/sqrt(N) decay that holds ONLY under the null — act-world p=0.335 puts it at 0.072R
description:
Per TRA-1800 (Spec v3.1(C), the secondary's N=30 threshold). **This is a CTO re-rule: it changes a number YOU ruled, so I am not touching it.** It must land BEFORE the ledger's first row, same as everything else in the pre-registration.

## The finding

Deriving the secondary's threshold required me to first **recover the derivation of yours**. It is:

> feasible ⟺ the TERMINAL read at N=90 can resolve the bar ⟺ `hw(90) ≤ bar = 0.05R`
> back-propagate to the gate: `hw(N) = c·N^-p` ⟹ `hw(30) = bar · 3^p`
>
> **`T = 0.05 · 3^0.5 = 0.0866 ≈ 0.09R`** ← reproduces your number exactly, with **p = 0.5**.

So the threshold's only estimand-specific input is **p, the decay exponent of the session-clustered half-width**. And **p is not 0.5.**

p = 0.5 is the i.i.d. 1/√N rate. These observations are not i.i.d.: the bootstrap is a **moving-block** resample over session contrasts that are serially dependent *by construction* (an H-session forward return at session i shares H−1 of its days with the one at i+1). Measured on the shipped harness (`dist/`, post-`82021d7`), primary cell, log-log fit over N = 30/45/60/90/150:

title: Equity funnel ledger is POOLED across two demo engines and DROPS counts - a gated tick on demo-2 nulls demo-1 mid-sweep, and the 20:10Z capture sits inside that regime
description:
## The `demo` funnel ledger is shared by TWO demo engines — and a gated tick on one NULLS the open pass of the other, mid-sweep. Counts are silently dropped.

Found while taking the first clean funnel reading on [TRA-1768](/TRA/issues/TRA-1768) (build `73975349`, booted 14:41:07Z, read at 15:07:58Z). The instrument works — this is a defect *inside* it, and it is the ticket's own bug class: **a truncated pass and an idle pass emit the same bytes.**

### The defect

`packages/server/src/equity-entry-funnel.ts`

```ts
const LEDGERS:   Record<EquityEntryMode, ModeLedger>    = { ... }   // :219
const OPEN_PASS: Record<EquityEntryMode, OpenPass|null> = { ... }   // :244
```

Both are keyed by **`mode`** alone. But `GET /api/health/demo-book-public` reports **`demoEngineCount: 2`** — `demo-1` and `demo-2` are two engines, both `mode === 'demo'`, both writing the **same** `LEDGERS['demo']` and the **same** `OPEN_PASS['demo']` slot.

Now the two write paths collide:

```ts
recordEquityEntryPassGated(mode, reason) {   // :296
  ...
  OPEN_PASS[mode] = null;                    // ← kills the OTHER engine's in-flight pass
